answer: Watermarked-challenge tracing resists sybil graders: each grading assignment carries a per-grader cryptographic watermark, so if identical grade rationales or copied answers surface across supposedly-independent graders, the shared watermark exposes one operator behind many keys. A beacon of the same pigment bleeding across a nebula of grader identities proves collusion that independent grading never produces. Tracing the watermark lineage flags the cluster and strips its standing; honest graders each carry unique, non-colliding marks.
